paragraphs.text: Play a short ding whenever DeepSeek Harness asks for tool approval.
# dsh-approval-ding
A short **ding** and a flashing taskbar button the moment DeepSeek Harness needs you: a tool-approva
l prompt, or a question.
审批提示音 + 任务栏闪烁：DeepSeek Harness 请求审批、或向你提问时响一声“叮”，同时任务栏图标像微信来消息那样闪烁。
## Why

When an agent calls a tool that needs permission, or stops to ask you something, DSH
waits silently.

If you have switched to another window or another app, the turn
stalls until you notice. This plugi

n plays a short bell as soon as the prompt
appears — before you have answered anything.

It never answers, approves, rejects or delays anything. It only asks for your
attention.
## What triggers it
| Trigger | When it fires |

| `approval/request` | A tool call needs your permission |
| `user-questions/request` | `ask_user_qu
estion` asks you something, including its timed variant and the `exit_plan_mode` plan review |
## Install
From GitHub:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or find it in the plugin market and install it there.
No build step, no dependencies — the package ships plain ESM and one WAV file.
## What you hear

`assets/ding.wav`: a 0.62 s bell at E6 (1318.51 Hz) with four inharmonic partials,
44.1 kHz mono 16-

ets/ding.wav`: a 0.62 s bell at E6 (1318.51 Hz) with four inharmonic partials,
44.1 kHz mono 16-bit.

`sound: system` uses the OS notification sound instead; any other value is treated
as a path to a `.
wav` (absolute, or relative to the package root).
## Taskbar attention (Windows)

Along with the ding, the DSH taskbar button blinks — the same way WeChat tells you
a message arrived

. While the window is in the background it keeps blinking until
you activate it; when it already has

focus, six short blinks make the prompt
noticeable without being noisy.

The plugin runs inside the Node-mode host process, which has no access to the
Electron window (`flas

hFrame` / `setOverlayIcon`), so the hint is done by a small
PowerShell helper: `FlashWindowEx` from

`user32`. No extra dependency, no shell
modification.

`badge: true` additionally pins a red exclamation overlay on the taskbar button
(`ITaskbarList3::Set

OverlayIcon`), cleared when the window comes to the foreground
or after `attentionTimeoutSeconds`. I

t is off by default because the overlay is
drawn by the shell on top of the app icon and looks heavy

for a keyboard-driven
workflow.
## Configuration
Every key is optional; the defaults are shown.

## How it works

- Two Cordis waterfalls are the triggers: **`approval/request`**, which DSH only
dispatches when a p

rompt is really needed (under a `never` approval policy the
request is rejected before the waterfall

runs, so the plugin stays silent), and
**`user-questions/request`**, which `ctx.userQuestions.ask()

` dispatches for every
question batch.
- Both listeners are registered with `{ prepend: true, global

: true }`: `global`
keeps a root-level listener visible to Agent-scoped dispatch, `prepend` makes it

run before any answerer (including the browser bridge that takes over the
composer), so the sound i

s not lost to a fast decision.
- They return `next()` untouched. The real answerers — the web approv

al panel, the
question card, a command-line prompt, another plugin — still receive the request
uncha

nged.
- Playback happens in a helper child process with `stdio: 'ignore'`, so a slow
PowerShell star

t or a missing audio device can never block the turn. Every
failure is swallowed: a failed ding must
not fail a request.
## Platform
| Platform | Playback |

| Windows | `powershell.exe` + `System.Media.SoundPlayer` |
| macOS | `afplay` |
| Linux | `paplay`,
falling back to `aplay` |

Taskbar attention is Windows-only. On macOS and Linux the plugin plays the sound
and leaves the dock

on is Windows-only. On macOS and Linux the plugin plays the sound
and leaves the dock/taskbar alone.

The sound is played on the machine that runs the DSH host process. If your browser
connects to a rem
ote host, the ding is heard on the host, not in the browser tab.

> Windows note: the helper must **not** be spawned with `detached: true`. A
> `DETACHED_PROCESS` `po

wershell.exe` starts without a console, exits 0
> immediately and never runs its script — verified:
no audio, no side effect.
## Latency

PowerShell cold start is roughly 0.5 s on Windows, so the ding is heard about half
a second after th

tart is roughly 0.5 s on Windows, so the ding is heard about half
a second after the prompt appears.
## Uninstall

Remove the bundle with the plugin manager, or drop `dsh-approval-ding` from
`dsh.profile.bundles` in
the profile's `package.json`.
